title: Carlton "Santa" Davis - Wikipedia
notes: Carlton Sylvester 'Santa' Davis, born 21 November 1953, Kingston (the page's category says 1950). Greenwich Farm; the nickname from a skating accident that left his face swollen and red. A Catholic church marching band from about ten, taught the rocksteady beat by Bobby Aitken; the Graduates at fourteen; the Rhythm Raiders with George 'Fully' Fullwood in 1969, soon the Soul Syndicate; Bunny Lee's Aggrovators in the 1970s; credited with helping popularise the 'flying cymbals' on Johnny Clarke's None Shall Escape the Judgement (1974), mixed by King Tubby; the Roots Radics; the film Rockers (1978); Survival and Confrontation for Bob Marley; Peter Tosh's band, wounded in the shooting in which Tosh was killed; Big Mountain; now Ziggy Marley's drummer. Over 200 drum credits, 1970-85.

title: Santa Davis - Remo artist profile
notes: Credits him with 'originating the flying cymbal sound' with the Aggrovators; names Coming In From the Cold, Chant Down Babylon and Africa Unite for Marley; Willie Nelson's Countryman (2005); Isaac Hayes, Carlos Santana, Chaka Khan, Pink. Remo heads: Pinstripe and Ambassador on the toms, Powerstroke P3 on the bass drum, Ambassador Coated.

title: Drummer Santa Davis' inspiring journey to Musgrave and Reggae Gold awards (Jamaica Gleaner, 7 April 2024)
notes: Seventy years old in 2024; joined the St Peter Claver Drum Corps at eleven, in 1964. Records: Africa Unite and Chant Down Babylon (Marley), Bunny Wailer's Liberation, Burning Spear's Marcus Garvey and Tradition, Dennis Brown's Money in My Pocket and West Bound Train; tours with Jimmy Cliff, Black Uhuru, Burning Spear, Big Youth, the Wailers, Big Mountain, Ziggy Marley, Peter Tosh. Bronze Musgrave Medal and a Reggae Gold Award, 2024. Lives in California.

title: The Day the Music Died in Kingston (Carlton "Santa" Davis as told to Larson Sutton, Relix, 3 May 2018)
notes: In his own words: the Soul Syndicate in the early 1970s; Wailers sessions with Lee Perry in 1971 (High Tide or Low Tide, Sun Is Shining, Mr. Brown); 'We recorded Ketchy Shuby, and it was terrific, but I'd already made a commitment to Jimmy Cliff' (1976), credited on Legalize It as 'Santa'; Tosh's band for the last six years of his life; shot in the clavicle on 11 September 1987, when Tosh, Free I and Doc Brown were killed.

title: I by I: Santa Davis on the flying cymbals (Fact magazine, 2 April 2016)
notes: He played the pattern on the hi-hat on None Shall Escape the Judgement at Treasure Isle, meaning it for that one song; it 'has been around for ages' (Lloyd Knibb, Earl Young of MFSB); Bunny Lee named it; 'Tubbys brought that cymbal to life'. Under it, 'on drums you'd still be doing a one drop'. Admires Carlton Barrett and Horsemouth Wallace. Ketchy Shuby (Legalize It, with Robbie Shakespeare); the Soul Syndicate's Sun Is Shining and Duppy Conqueror; Africa Unite and Coming In From the Cold. Tosh took him on in 1981 after Sly Dunbar left: 'I want you to saddle up.'

title: The (Not So Clear-Cut) History of the Flying Cymbal (Red Bull Music Academy Daily, July 2013)
notes: Davis, the Aggrovators' main drummer, on adapting MFSB's The Sound of Philadelphia ('Damn, let's try that in a reggae sound') in a 1974 jam that gave Johnny Clarke None Shall Escape the Judgement; Clarke recalls him playing the cymbal as a warm-up; Bunny Lee named it and wanted it 'in every song'. Sly Dunbar says he heard it first on Moonlight Lover and played it with Skin, Flesh and Bones ('MFSB got it from us'). Flying-cymbal records of 1974-75: Joshua's Word, Move Out of Babylon, Enter His Gates With Praise (Clarke), Cornell Campbell's The Gorgon, Linval Thompson's Kung Fu Man.

title: Carlton "Santa" Davis: everything has come full circle (Jah Rebel, Reggae.be, 27 November 2012)
notes: 'I didn't really create that flying cymbal riff; it was already done by a guy called Hugh Malcolm' (Moonlight Lover); tried at a Bunny Lee session at Treasure Isle for None Shall Escape the Judgement. Names Mama Africa (Tosh, 1983) and, for Marley, Coming In From the Cold, Chant Down Babylon and Africa Unite.

title: Carlton Santa Davis - Couleur Café, June 2011 (Rebel Base)
notes: The same account of the flying cymbal and the same records named; the St Peter Claver Drum Corps; no kit of his own as a boy.

title: Santa Davis Shares Interesting Story Of Bob Marley Asking Him To Play Drums On 'Africa Unite' (I Never Knew TV, YouTube)
notes: Waiting at Tuff Gong for a Burning Spear session, Marley called him in to play Africa Unite; Coming In From the Cold too. 'Me, I was kind of like a wild kind of drummer, I would do stuff really aggressive, but Bob Marley was really laid back.' (Auto-captions, read for the gist.)

title: Word, Sound and Power - Wikipedia
notes: Tosh's band. Santa Davis on drums from late 1981 to 1983 (the Wanted Dread and Alive tour, the Mama Africa album and tour) and again shortly before Tosh's death in 1987; earlier he and Fully Fullwood stood in when Sly and Robbie toured with Black Uhuru.

title: Legalize It - Wikipedia
notes: Peter Tosh's first solo album, June 1976 (Virgin, Columbia), recorded at Treasure Isle and Randy's, Kingston, 1975-76. Drums: Carlton 'Santa' Davis and Carlton Barrett, tracks not divided. Ketchy Shuby 4:53.

title: Mama Africa (Peter Tosh album) - Wikipedia
notes: 1983, EMI; recorded 1982-83; produced by Chris Kimsey and Tosh. Drums: Carlton 'Santa' Davis and Sly Dunbar; bass Leebert 'Gibby' Morrison and Robbie Shakespeare. Mama Africa 7:56.

title: No Nuclear War - Wikipedia
notes: 1987, Tosh's last album. Carlton 'Santa' Davis, drums (the only drummer listed); bass Danny Thompson, Fully Fullwood, Gibby Morrison. No Nuclear War 7:57.

title: Confrontation (Bob Marley and the Wailers album) - Wikipedia
notes: 23 May 1983, compiled after Marley's death from material of c. 1977-80 finished at Tuff Gong in 1982. Drums: Carlton Barrett; Carlton 'Santa' Davis on Chant Down Babylon (2:36).

title: Complete Captured Live 1984 (petertosh.com)
notes: Recorded at the Greek Theatre, Los Angeles, in 1983, issued as a single LP of highlights in 1984; Bush Doctor among the tracks. The concert film shows the drummer at a big kit of red shells with chrome rims.
